Description: Company logo, company name, and first-page branding/header. This is the first-page-only format that Huzaifa described as the title-block / cover-page layout.
Notes / Open Questions: Keep as template-driven. Only page 1 uses the full logo/header treatment.

Description: Office list and phone-number footer used on the first page.
Notes / Open Questions: Separate from later-page footer because page 2+ follows a different format.

Description: Top-right office address block. Transcript says focus Edmonton first; other offices can be added later without changing overall layout.
Notes / Open Questions: Use Edmonton office block for the first V1 template.

Description: Date the letter is written, not necessarily the same as inspection date.
Notes / Open Questions: User-selected date field.

Description: File No. line under the letter date.
Notes / Open Questions: Pulled from inspection metadata in later phases; manually entered/selected in first generator.

Description: Client name (bold) plus mailing-address block immediately above the Re: section.
Notes / Open Questions: Client master list later; manual/dropdown in early V1.

Description: Base heading is “Foundation Soil Inspection”; transcript allows an optional dash suffix for rarer cases.
Notes / Open Questions: Default to base heading; optional manual suffix field.

Description: Lot / Block / Plan line for the inspected property.
Notes / Open Questions: Lot and block may be short numeric values; plan may be letters/numbers. Option for letters/number available for all (lot, block, plan). Lot and block can be up to 3 characters with letters or/and numbers. The plan is 3 charcters followed by a space then 4 more characters (mixture of letters and numbers).

Description: Street/civic address of the inspected site.
Bedrock-style extra job-number line below street address.
Notes / Open Questions: Default off. Exposed only when needed for clients such as Bedrock.

Description: Subdivision name, usually present.
Notes / Open Questions: Default on; allow omission when unknown.

Description: City / municipality line, Edmonton by default but selectable for other municipalities.
Notes / Open Questions: Dropdown candidate: Edmonton, Sherwood Park, Spruce Grove, etc.

Description: Default intro paragraph describing the purpose of inspection and ABC assumption. Normal path inserts inspection date; special follow-up mode can replace the whole intro.
Notes / Open Questions: Normal V1 uses the standard intro. Frost follow-up remains a special replacement path, not a second paragraph.

Description: Starts with a fixed excavation sentence, then cut range, then optional excavation add-ons such as garage same elevation, garage higher than house, walkout wording, already-poured footing wording, and observed site issues, over excavated trench, frost issues, organic fill or engineered fill by others comments, etc.
Notes / Open Questions: P2 is the main logic driver. Order matters: base excavation -> cut/walkout wording -> garage append (if any) -> other observed issue clauses.

Description: Soil description paragraph built from structured descriptors: origin (main: native or engineered fill or combination of both), material type (clay (either silty, sandy, or both), sand (course grain, medium grain, fine grain, loose compaction, very loose, compact, dense, very dense compaction, well graded, poorly graded), silt (same compaction options as sand and very fine grain), very sandy, very silty, silty to very silty, sandy to very sandy, or select multiple), moisture (damp, moist, very moist, wet, able to pick 2 with scaling (going left to right on linear scale without skipping)), colour (brown, grey, brown and grey, brown and dark grey, dark grey, black, reddish-brown), plasticity (low plastic, medium plastic, and high plastic or again on a linear scale (low to med or med to high)), density/consistency, traces, engineered-fill provenance, and high-plastic warning when triggered.
Notes / Open Questions: P3 should be structured from controlled selections, not free text. 'Native deposit' wording only appears when the soil is actually native.

Description: Main house-footing recommendation. Can resolve to standard, modified, or as-constructed adequacy wording, and may prepend conditional language tied to excavation/soil issues.
Notes / Open Questions: Paragraph 4 is driven by selections in P2 and P3; spread-footing sentence lives here as an add-on.

Description: Separate garage recommendation paragraph added only when garage conditions apply.
Notes / Open Questions: If P2 says a garage exists, P5 must appear. Garden-suite mode is special and uses P5 without the normal house P4 path.

Description: One-of-four sulphate-result paragraph: negligible, moderate, severe, or very severe.
Notes / Open Questions: Huzaifa describes this as a simple add-on paragraph.

Description: Standard winter-construction paragraph appended after the technical recommendation paragraphs.
Notes / Open Questions: Keep always-on in V1. If later evidence proves otherwise, this can be relaxed in a later version.

Description: Standard closing: “We trust this information is considered satisfactory...”
Prepared-by name and designation, with blank signing space above.
Notes / Open Questions: Prepared-by block is optional. When the author is already the signing engineer, the standard engineer block can absorb the author/signer identity.

Description: Reviewer name, stamp image, and member number area.
Notes / Open Questions: Standard V1 output should always include the engineer signoff/stamp block. Image asset, name, designation, and member number are variable.

Description: Blank permit-to-practice signing area kept in the fixed V1 output. It is not tied to the selected engineer stamp.
Notes / Open Questions: Second call says this should be a single fixed blank permit-to-practice asset that can be signed by an eligible director/signatory.

Description: H-drive path printed at the bottom for filing/reference.
Notes / Open Questions: Derived from year + housing folder + client folder + generated filename. Hidden H number appears here, not in visible body text.

Description: Page 2+ layout uses the later-page header/footer style, not the page-1 title-block style.
Notes / Open Questions: Template must use a different first page.
